patients.summary: Teacher who joins in 2021 with three-drug hypertension found to be primary hyperaldosteronism, just before thyroidectomy for papillary thyroid cancer. Later a fibroadenoma, a right frontal meningioma resected in 2024, and an anterior communicating aneurysm rupture coiled in late 2024, with a second thunderclap admission in 2025 that excluded a bleed.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 42F, teacher, here to establish and for a BP letter. Her new district's pre-employment exam read her pressure as high. Says she has been treated for 'high blood pressure' for about four years at her old office, on lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5 and HCTZ 25, takes them every day. Also tired for months and gets cramps in her calves and hands, worse at the end of the school day, sometimes at night.

Other history per pt (records requested): fibroids with heavy periods, seen on an ultrasound a couple of years ago; her old PCP felt a lump in her neck this spring, ultrasound then needle biopsy in May came back papillary thyroid cancer. She has a surgeon and the thyroidectomy is set for mid-July. Tylenol now and then for a headache.
No drug allergies. Never smoked, doesn't drink. Single, lives alone, teaches 2nd grade.
Family: mother had breast cancer at 58. Father has hypertension and had a brain aneurysm. A sister on thyroid replacement.

Exam: BP 158/100 (repeat similar), HR 76. Well appearing. Small firm nodule R thyroid lobe, no nodes. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. No edema. Neuro grossly intact.

A/P
1. Hypertension, uncontrolled on 3 agents incl a diuretic, with cramps and fatigue. Needs a secondary workup. BMP today, and renin/aldosterone drawn this morning (pt on ACEi, which if anything raises renin). Will call with results. No med change today.
2. Papillary thyroid ca on FNA, surgery scheduled. Asked her to have the surgeon's office send the op note.
3. Fibroids - symptomatic, she'd like to talk to GYN after the summer.
4. Health maintenance: records pending. Will do full physical in the winter.
Letter for school: under care for blood pressure, cleared to work.

documents.title: Lab result note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: K 3.1, bicarb 31, Na 146. Hypokalemic alkalosis on HCTZ with BP this high - aldosteronism high on the list. Waiting on renin/aldo before adding anything.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Summary of records received (scanned, 41 pages).
Hypertension diagnosed 2017; lisinopril, then amlodipine added 2018, HCTZ added 2020. No secondary workup in the records.
Pelvic ultrasound 09/2019: enlarged fibroid uterus.
Thyroid ultrasound 04/2021: 2.4 cm solid hypoechoic nodule right lobe. FNA 05/11/2021: papillary thyroid carcinoma. Referred to endocrine surgery.
Screening: cervical cytology with HPV 03/2020 negative. Screening mammogram 02/2020 negative.
Allergies: NKDA.
Reviewed by PCP.

conditions.label: Resistant hypertension secondary to primary hyperaldosteronism

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (50 mg) by mouth daily

orders.reason: primary hyperaldosteronism; thyroid cancer after surgery

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Renin activity undetectable, aldosterone 31. With the low K this is primary aldosteronism - explains the cramps and why three meds weren't touching her pressure. Explained in plain terms: the adrenal glands making too much of a salt-retaining hormone. Starting spironolactone 50 daily (2 x 25 mg), keep the other three for now. Possible side effects reviewed (breast tenderness, irregular bleeding, dizziness). Repeat BMP in about 10 days. Endocrinology referral placed - same group can see her for the thyroid after surgery. She was relieved there is a reason. Sent to pharmacy.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: K up to 4.0 on spironolactone. Good. Message sent to pt.

documents.title: Endocrine surgery discharge summary
documents.author: endocrine surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, endocrine surgery service. Admitted 07/12/2021, discharged 07/13/2021.
Procedure 07/12/2021: total thyroidectomy for FNA-proven papillary thyroid carcinoma, right lobe. Both recurrent laryngeal nerves identified and preserved. Parathyroids identified in situ.
Postoperative course uncomplicated. Voice normal. Calcium normal on serial checks, no symptoms of hypocalcemia.
Discharge medications: levothyroxine 100 mcg daily (new); continue lisinopril 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, spironolactone 50 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: final pathology to endocrinology; endocrinology appointment early September.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks out from thyroidectomy, went home next day. Voice fine, no tingling. Started levothyroxine 100.
On spironolactone 6 wks. Cramps are gone, she says she hadn't realized how tired she was until it lifted. No breast tenderness or dizziness. Home readings mostly 130s/80s.
Exam: BP a little higher here than her home log. Incision clean, well healed, no swelling. Lungs clear, RRR, no edema.
A/P: Primary aldosteronism - much better on spironolactone; K was 4.0. Continue all four. Endo appt 9/2 will cover adrenal imaging and post-op thyroid. Thyroid ca - path pending with surgeon/endo. RTC 3-4 months.

medications.reason: after total thyroidectomy for papillary carcinoma

reports.text:
Specimen: thyroid, total thyroidectomy.
Papillary thyroid carcinoma, classic type, right lobe, 2.5 cm in greatest dimension. Vascular invasion present. No extrathyroidal extension. Margins negative. Lymph nodes: none involved. Left lobe and isthmus: no tumor.
reports.conclusion: Papillary thyroid carcinoma, 2.5 cm, with vascular invasion; margins negative; no lymph node involvement.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group. Date of visit 09/02/2021.
Reason: referred by PCP for primary aldosteronism; post total thyroidectomy (07/12/2021) for papillary thyroid carcinoma.
She is doing well since surgery, no complaints, and came with a list of questions about what she can do to keep the cancer from coming back.
Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg, spironolactone 50 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, HCTZ 25 mg, acetaminophen PRN. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: neck incision healing well, no erythema, drainage or collection. No palpable cervical nodes.
Labs: TSH 15. Thyroglobulin undetectable.
Pathology: 2.5 cm papillary carcinoma, vascular invasion, nodes negative.
Assessment/Plan:
1. Papillary thyroid carcinoma s/p total thyroidectomy. Intermediate features (vascular invasion) but node negative and an undetectable thyroglobulin. We talked through radioactive iodine at length; given the undetectable thyroglobulin we agreed together to forgo it and follow her closely. TSH is too high on 100 mcg - increase levothyroxine to 125 mcg. Aim for TSH in the low-normal range. Recheck TSH in 6-7 weeks (can be drawn at PCP). Thyroglobulin and neck ultrasound yearly.
2. Primary aldosteronism, confirmed biochemically by PCP (suppressed renin, aldosterone 31, hypokalemia). Adrenal CT ordered to look for a unilateral adenoma. Continue spironolactone 50 mg meanwhile.
Copy to PCP.

documents.title: CT adrenal glands without and with contrast
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
Outside imaging center. Exam date 09/20/2021.
Indication: primary aldosteronism.
Technique: thin-section CT through the adrenal glands before and after IV contrast.
Findings: Right adrenal gland normal in size and contour. Left adrenal gland normal in size and contour. No adrenal nodule. Visualized kidneys, liver and pancreas unremarkable.
Impression: Normal adrenal glands. No adrenal nodule.

documents.title: Endocrinology addendum
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Addendum to 09/02/2021 consult. Adrenal CT shows normal glands with no nodule. In the setting of confirmed primary aldosteronism this most likely represents bilateral disease, which is treated medically. Plan lifelong mineralocorticoid antagonist - continue spironolactone 50 mg daily, potassium and creatinine with her PCP. Will see her in a year with thyroglobulin and neck ultrasound.

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal views. Uterus enlarged with multiple intramural fibroids, the largest 5.1 cm in the fundus. Endometrium normal thickness. Ovaries normal. No free fluid.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology, date of visit 10/07/2021.
Self-referred, PCP copied. Long history of heavy periods with known fibroids; soaks through protection on the first two days, misses work. Wants a uterus-sparing option and a short recovery; no plans for pregnancy.
Ultrasound today: enlarged fibroid uterus, largest 5.1 cm fundal intramural.
Options reviewed: hormonal options, myomectomy, hysterectomy, uterine artery embolization. She prefers embolization. Referred to interventional radiology; tentatively scheduled over the late November break.
Allergies NKDA.

documents.title: Nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In after school for flu vaccine, L deltoid, tolerated. Lot recorded. TSH drawn per endo request on the new 125 dose. Pt reports COVID primary series done in the spring through the school district clinic, card shown.

documents.title: TSH result

documents.body: TSH 1.4 on levothyroxine 125. Right where endo wants it. Copy to endocrinology.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, seen with gynecology. Date of visit 12/02/2021.
CC: lower abdominal pain and vaginal discharge, 2 days after uterine artery embolization (11/30/2021).
HPI: 43F with primary aldosteronism and prior papillary thyroid cancer s/p thyroidectomy. Cramping lower abdominal pain since the procedure, steadily worse over two days, with a light blood-tinged discharge. No fever, nausea, vomiting or diarrhea.
Meds: spironolactone, lisinopril, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide, levothyroxine, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.
Vitals: T 37.2, BP 130/85, P 88, RR 16.
Exam: abdomen with a tender, enlarged uterus, no rebound or guarding. Pelvic: small amount of blood-tinged discharge, no foul odor. 
Labs: WBC 9.0, Hgb 12.5, Plt 250. CRP 8 (ref <5). Urine hCG negative.
ED course: ketorolac 15 mg IV with good relief. Reviewed with gynecology - presentation consistent with post-embolization syndrome, no features of infection.
Dx: post-embolization syndrome.
Dispo: home. Ibuprofen 600 mg q6h PRN with food up to a week. Return for fever, foul discharge, heavy bleeding or worsening pain. PCP follow-up within a week.

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from home after school, identity verified. ED last Thursday for pain two days after her fibroid embolization - post-embolization syndrome. Pain has eased a lot, only needed ibuprofen twice yesterday, none today. Discharge tapering off. No fever.
Reminded her: ibuprofen only short term with her BP meds and spironolactone - she has stopped.
A/P: post-embolization syndrome, resolving. GYN follow-up already booked January. Call for fever or heavy bleeding.

documents.title: Gynecology follow-up
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: Outside gynecology, visit 01/11/2022. Six weeks after uterine artery embolization (11/30/2021). ED visit two days post procedure for post-embolization syndrome, settled with NSAIDs. First period since was noticeably lighter, about four days, no clots, did not miss work. Abdomen soft, nontender. Plan: no further intervention; will reassess if bleeding returns. Back to routine gynecologic care with PCP. NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 43F. Feeling well. Energy good since spironolactone. Periods lighter since the embolization in Nov. No headaches beyond the odd one from grading late. Home BP mostly 128-136 / 80s.
Meds: spironolactone 50, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, levothyroxine 125, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.
Social: teaching 2nd grade at the new school, likes it. Walks after work. Never smoker, no alcohol.
Family: mother breast ca at 58; father HTN and cerebral aneurysm; sister hypothyroid.
ROS negative.
Exam: well. Thyroidectomy scar healed. Breasts symmetric, no masses, no nipple change, axillae clear. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin unremarkable.
A/P
- Primary aldosteronism / resistant HTN: at goal-ish at home. CMP today for K and Cr.
- PTC s/p thyroidectomy: endo yearly, TSH today.
- Fibroids s/p UAE: improved.
- Screening: Tdap today. HCV and HIV screening today. Cervical co-test due 2025. Mammogram - mother's history; she's had one in 2020, order screening yearly - she'd like to wait until summer when school is out.
- Flu given in the fall; COVID booster discussed.

documents.title: Annual labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CMP, CBC, lipids, TSH normal. K normal on spironolactone + lisinopril. HCV and HIV nonreactive. Portal message sent.

documents.title: Refills

documents.body: Hi, could I get 90 day refills on the spironolactone and the levothyroxine? My insurance changed the mail order rules. Thank you!

documents.title: Re: Refills

documents.body: Hi Ms. Reed, 90-day supplies of both sent to the mail order pharmacy with 3 refills. Let us know if they don't arrive within 10 days.

conditions.label: Lump in right breast, upper outer quadrant

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - breast lump
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Found a lump in her right breast in the shower about a month ago. Has not changed since. Not painful. No discharge from the nipple, no skin dimpling or redness. She has been checking it every day and admits she is scared - mother's cancer, plus her own thyroid cancer last year. Sleeping less. GAD-7 8.
Exam: firm mass about 1.5 cm R breast upper outer quadrant, does not move freely, nontender. No skin changes, no nipple retraction. No axillary or supraclavicular nodes. L breast normal.
A/P
1. Palpable R breast mass. Diagnostic mammogram + targeted ultrasound, marked urgent. Explained most lumps at her age turn out benign but this one needs imaging and likely a biopsy.
2. Situational anxiety around the lump. Talked it through; she'd rather not start anything, has her sister for support. Will move quickly so she's not waiting. Message me anytime.

reports.text: Bilateral diagnostic mammogram with spot compression of the right breast. Breasts heterogeneously dense. A BB marker at the palpable site, right breast upper outer quadrant, overlies an oval circumscribed equal-density mass. No suspicious calcifications. Left breast: no mass, distortion or suspicious calcifications.
reports.conclusion: Oval circumscribed mass at the palpable site, right breast. See ultrasound.

reports.text: Targeted right breast ultrasound at the palpable site. At 10 o'clock, 6 cm from the nipple: oval, circumscribed, hypoechoic solid mass, parallel orientation, 1.6 x 1.0 x 1.2 cm. No posterior shadowing. Right axilla: normal lymph nodes.
reports.conclusion: 1.6 cm solid mass, right breast 10 o'clock, corresponding to the palpable finding. BI-RADS 4A: low suspicion for malignancy. Ultrasound-guided core biopsy recommended.

conditions.label: Lump in right breast, upper outer quadrant

reports.text:
Specimen: right breast, 10 o'clock, ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (4 cores).
Fibroadenoma. No atypia. No malignancy identified.

documents.title: Breast biopsy report
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
Outside breast imaging center. Ultrasound-guided core biopsy, right breast 10 o'clock, 14-gauge, 4 cores, 06/28/2022. Clip placed, confirmed on post-procedure mammogram. No complications.
Addendum 07/01: pathology fibroadenoma, benign and concordant with imaging. Recommend follow-up right breast ultrasound in 6 months, then annual screening mammography.

documents.title: Biopsy result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called with path: fibroadenoma, benign. She cried with relief. Follow-up ultrasound in 6 months per radiology, then yearly mammograms. Ordered.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, visit 09/13/2022.
One year after total thyroidectomy for 2.5 cm PTC (vascular invasion, N0), no RAI. Feels well. Benign breast biopsy this summer.
Levothyroxine 125 mcg; TSH in range today. Thyroglobulin <0.1. Neck ultrasound 09/08: empty thyroid bed, no abnormal nodes.
Excellent response to therapy. Continue current dose; yearly TSH, thyroglobulin and ultrasound.
Aldosteronism: on spironolactone 50 with lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ. K and creatinine normal today. BP 134/84 here. Continue. Return 1 year.

orders.reason: progressive headaches with nocturnal and positional features, morning vomiting

documents.title: Office Visit - headaches
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Headaches since late summer, close to three months. Dull, all over the front, worse at night and when she bends to help the kids at their desks. Some mornings nauseated and has vomited a few times before work. Acetaminophen takes the edge off. Never had headaches like this.
BP fine at home. No fever, no trauma.
Exam: BP normal. Alert, fluent. Cranial nerves grossly intact. Moves all limbs; gait normal.
A/P: new progressive headache with nighttime/positional worsening and morning vomiting - red flags. Urgent neurology referral today for evaluation and brain imaging; called the neurology office myself to get her in. ED if sudden severe headache, weakness, vision change or confusion. Acetaminophen as needed in the meantime.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology, visit 12/12/2022. Urgent referral from PCP.
44F with primary aldosteronism and papillary thyroid carcinoma treated by thyroidectomy in 2021. Three months of dull aching headache, worse at night and on bending forward, with nausea and some morning vomiting.
Meds: spironolactone, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, levothyroxine, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.
Exam: BP normal. Mild left-sided weakness, 4+/5 arm and leg. Slight tremor of the left hand. Rest of the neuro exam normal.
MRI brain with and without contrast (same day): 2 cm enhancing right frontal lobe mass with vasogenic edema.
Impression: right frontal brain mass with edema explaining her headache and left-sided signs.
Plan: dexamethasone 4 mg twice daily, tapering over 4 weeks. Urgent neurosurgery referral placed. No driving until neurosurgery has seen her. Return for worse headache, vomiting, weakness or seizure.

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, at home. Neurology letter and MRI reviewed with her: 2 cm right frontal mass with edema. On dexamethasone a week - headache much better, no vomiting since Wednesday, says the left hand feels steadier. Some trouble sleeping on the steroid. Neurosurgery appt Jan 10.
Taking the week off before break; colleagues covering. Mother staying with her.
A/P: R frontal mass - added to list. Steroid: take with food, take the dose by early afternoon. Watch BP and sugars while on it - no symptoms of high sugar. Let me know what neurosurgery says. ED precautions reviewed.

reports.text: Right breast 10 o'clock: biopsy-proven fibroadenoma, oval circumscribed hypoechoic mass, 1.6 x 1.0 x 1.1 cm, unchanged. Biopsy clip in place.
reports.conclusion: Stable biopsy-proven fibroadenoma. BI-RADS 2: benign. Return to annual screening mammography.

documents.title: Neurosurgery consultation
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Outside neurosurgery, visit 01/10/2023.
44F referred by neurology for a 2 cm enhancing right frontal mass with vasogenic edema (MRI 12/12/2022), found on workup of three months of headache with mild left-sided weakness and left-hand tremor. On a dexamethasone taper; headache gone, weakness and tremor resolved.
PMH: primary aldosteronism; papillary thyroid cancer, thyroidectomy 2021, no evidence of disease.
Exam today: neuro intact, strength 5/5 throughout, no tremor.
Imaging reviewed: the appearance favors a meningioma.
Discussion: offered resection now versus surveillance MRI now that she is asymptomatic. She wishes to avoid surgery if she can and to finish the school year. Reasonable. Repeat MRI in 3 months; sooner for any recurrent headache, weakness or seizure. Finish the steroid taper. OK to drive.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 44F. Off dexamethasone since mid-January, no headaches. Neurosurgery watching the R frontal mass, repeat MRI in April. Back at work fully. Worry about the mass comes and goes; sleeping better. GAD-7 4.
Meds: spironolactone 50, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, levothyroxine 125, acetaminophen PRN.
Exam: well appearing. Neuro: strength symmetric, no tremor, gait normal. Breasts: small firm mobile R UOQ lump at the biopsy site, unchanged; no other masses. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abd benign, no edema.
A/P
- R frontal mass, likely meningioma per neurosurgery: on surveillance.
- Aldosteronism/HTN: stable, CMP today.
- Hx PTC: endo yearly.
- Fibroadenoma R breast: stable on Jan US. Screening mammogram this summer.
- Colorectal screening at 45 - next year.
Labs today.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit 12/14/2023.
CC: severe headaches, morning nausea, blurry vision.
HPI: 45F with a known right frontal mass on surveillance and primary aldosteronism. Over recent weeks her headaches have become severe and throbbing, felt at the back of the head, daily and worst on waking, with nausea and vomiting most mornings. Brief episodes of blurred vision. No head injury, no new medications.
Meds: spironolactone, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, levothyroxine, acetaminophen. NKDA.
Vitals: BP 142/88, HR 78. BMI 30.
Exam: bilateral papilledema on fundoscopy. Remainder of neurologic exam unremarkable.
MRI brain: known right frontal mass, now with more surrounding edema.
ED diagnosis: structural intracranial lesion with raised pressure signs.
Course: dexamethasone 10 mg IV. Headache improved. Discussed with on-call neurosurgery, who know her - plan resection; to be scheduled within weeks.
Dispo: home on dexamethasone 4 mg twice daily until surgery. Return for worsening headache, vomiting, vision loss, weakness or seizure.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in ED last Thursday - several weeks of worsening morning headaches with vomiting and blurred vision; papilledema; MRI known R frontal mass with more edema. Back on dexamethasone 4 bid. Neurosurgery booked craniotomy Jan 9.
Today: headaches much less, no vomiting since steroid. Vision clear. Nervous about surgery but says it's a relief to have a plan. On leave from school until after recovery.
Exam: alert, neuro nonfocal, strength 5/5.
A/P: R frontal mass - surgery 1/9. Steroid precautions as before. Pre-op labs will be done by neurosurgery. Will see her after.

documents.title: Neurosurgery discharge summary
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, neurosurgery service. Admitted 01/09/2024, discharged 01/12/2024.
Indication: 2 cm enhancing right frontal mass on surveillance since 12/2022, now with increasing edema, papilledema and morning headaches with vomiting.
Procedure 01/09/2024: right frontal craniotomy, gross total resection.
Pathology: meningioma, WHO grade 1.
Course: uncomplicated. Neuro exam intact post-op. Headache controlled with acetaminophen. Wound clean.
Discharge meds: dexamethasone taper over 2 weeks then stop; acetaminophen PRN; home spironolactone, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, levothyroxine unchanged. NKDA.
Follow-up: staple removal at 10-14 days; MRI brain in 3 months; no driving for 2 weeks; return to work when cleared.

documents.title: Neurocritical care discharge summary
documents.author: neurocritical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital, neuro ICU. Admitted 11/28/2024 via the emergency department, discharged 12/09/2024.
Presentation: 46F, sudden severe headache - the worst of her life - while lifting a heavy box about 2 hours before arrival, with nausea and light sensitivity. History of right frontal meningioma resected 01/2024 (outside lists still say 'frontal lobe mass'), primary aldosteronism, PTC s/p thyroidectomy, fibroids s/p UAE. Father with a cerebral aneurysm.
ED: BP 158/94, HR 88. Alert, anxious, neck stiff.
CT head: no hemorrhage; postoperative craniotomy changes only.
Lumbar puncture: opening pressure 28 cm H2O. RBC 1500 tube 1, 1480 tube 4. Xanthochromia present. WBC 4. Protein 45. Glucose 60.
CT angiography: 6 mm saccular aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery.
Diagnosis: subarachnoid hemorrhage from ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm.
Course: endovascular coil embolization 11/29/2024, complete occlusion, no complications. Neuro ICU monitoring; nimodipine 60 mg every 4 hours for 21 days; no clinical vasospasm. Headache improved steadily. BP managed on home regimen. No neurologic deficit.
Discharge meds: nimodipine 60 mg q4h through 12/19/2024; acetaminophen PRN; spironolactone 50, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, hydrochlorothiazide 25, levothyroxine 125 unchanged. NKDA.
Follow-up: neurointerventional with angiogram in 6 months; PCP within 1 week; no heavy lifting for 4 weeks; no driving until cleared.

documents.title: Transitional care visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Home a week after 11 days in the neuro ICU for a ruptured anterior communicating aneurysm, coiled 11/29. Discharge summary reviewed. RN called her the day after discharge.
Headache now mild, acetaminophen once a day. No vomiting, no weakness, no confusion. Taking nimodipine every 4 hours - alarms on her phone, through 12/19. Some lightheadedness standing; home BP 118-126/76-80 on nimodipine plus her usual four.
Sister staying with her. Out of work through January.
Exam: BP below, alert, oriented, speech fluent. Pupils equal. Strength full, no drift. Gait steady.
A/P
1. Aneurysmal SAH, coiled. Finish nimodipine 12/19. Rise slowly from sitting; lightheadedness should ease once nimodipine stops - call if she feels faint. Angiogram in 6 months per neurointerventional. No heavy lifting.
2. Aldosteronism/HTN: as above. BMP drawn.
3. Meningioma s/p resection: MRI Jan.
Work note given. Call with any sudden headache.

documents.body:
Outside neurointerventional service. Diagnostic cerebral angiogram 06/10/2025, right femoral access.
Indication: 6-month follow-up after coil embolization of a ruptured anterior communicating artery aneurysm (11/29/2024).
Findings: coiled anterior communicating artery aneurysm completely occluded, no neck remnant. No other aneurysm. Normal intracranial circulation.
No complications; access site hemostasis with closure device.
Plan: noninvasive vascular imaging in 18 months.

documents.title: Neurocritical care discharge summary
documents.author: neurocritical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital, neuro ICU. Admitted 12/05/2025 via ED, discharged 12/07/2025.
Presentation: 47F with prior aneurysmal SAH (AComm, coiled 11/2024) and resected right frontal meningioma. Abrupt severe headache about two hours before arrival while gardening, similar to the prior bleed, with nausea and one episode of vomiting at home. No trauma or fall.
ED: BP 158/94, HR 88, T 37.1. Alert, anxious. Nonfocal neurologic exam. Neck stiff on flexion. Fundi normal.
CT head: no hemorrhage or mass effect.
With high suspicion for recurrent hemorrhage: lumbar puncture - opening pressure 17 cm H2O, RBC 6 tube 1 and 2 tube 4, no xanthochromia, WBC 1, protein 34, glucose 63. CT angiography: coiled aneurysm remains completely occluded, no new aneurysm, no vasospasm.
Assessment: subarachnoid hemorrhage excluded.
Course: admitted to neuro ICU for monitoring overnight. Headache settled with acetaminophen and ondansetron. Neuro checks stable. Transferred to floor 12/06, home 12/07.
Discharge meds: home meds unchanged (spironolactone 50, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, hydrochlorothiazide 25, levothyroxine 125, acetaminophen PRN). NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within a week; neurointerventional as scheduled.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Admitted Fri 12/5 for a sudden severe headache while gardening; two nights in neuro ICU. CT, LP and CTA all reassuring - no new bleed, coils holding. Summary reviewed with her.
Headache gone since Sunday. Shaken - 'it felt exactly like last time.' Back at school Monday.
Exam: alert, neuro intact, no meningismus today.
A/P: thunderclap headache with SAH excluded on full workup. Told her she did exactly the right thing going in and should do the same again. Aldosteronism/HTN - home readings back to her usual. No med changes. Physical in the summer.
